cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to all in Rome who are loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a big chain: those God called, He justified, and those He justified, He glorified (Romans 8:30). Now Paul stops and asks, "What then shall we say in response to these things?"

cards.question: Paul's next line starts with "If God is for us…" What does Paul say follows from that?

answers.text: No one can stand against us
Everyone will be on our side

cards.text: Then Paul points to the biggest gift there is. God did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all.

cards.question: God already gave up His own Son for us all. So what does Paul say God will also do?

answers.text: Ask us to pay Him back
Hold back the rest for now

cards.text: Friend, if somebody hands you the keys to the WHOLE bakery, you don't stand there sweating about one sprinkle. Then Paul asks, "Who will bring any charge against God’s elect?"

cards.question: Who will bring any charge against God's elect? What answer does Paul give?

answers.text: Their good works speak for them

cards.text: Next question: "Who is there to condemn us?" Paul points to Christ Jesus, who died, was raised to life, and is at the right hand of God.

cards.question: At the right hand of God, Paul says Christ Jesus is ___ for us.

cards.text: Now Paul asks the big one: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" And he lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword.

cards.question: Paul lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword. What kind of things are on that list?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Scriptures (Psalm 44:22): "For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered." Heavy line, friend.

cards.question: True or false: after that whole list, Paul says trouble, famine or sword can separate us from the love of Christ.
In all those hard things, what does Paul say we are through Him who loved us?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers," and he's not done yet.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the future might someday be able to separate us from God's love.
Paul adds height and depth. Then he says nothing else in all ___ will be able to separate us from the love of God.
True or false: Paul ends by saying this love of God is found in Christ Jesus our Lord.

findings.problem: Most story cards have no Papa Dorin voice at all. Cards 1, 3, 7, 9 and 14 are plain retellings. The walkthrough's only real joke is on card 5, and the only other reaction is "Heavy line, friend" on card 11. The cards read as a neutral summary, not as Papa Dorin telling the passage, and they never reach laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Across the walkthrough, Papa Dorin is at most mildly pleasant. Almost no reactions, comparisons, disbelief or self-deprecation go with the passage's big moments. Examples are God not sparing His own Son, the list of hardships, "more than conquerors" and nothing in all creation.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Everyone will be on our side" is close in meaning to the right answer "No one can stand against us." A baker could argue that if no one can be against us, everyone is effectively on our side.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
